Read-only review of Zoomies for a noncoder asking whether it has deep or shallow modules in John Ousterhout's sense: a simple interface hides substantial useful complexity. A visually tidy floorplan was generated grouping files by job, but this does not prove boundaries. Inspect actual code and callers. Do not judge quality by lines alone. No changes, no further delegation, no branches/worktrees. Existing user changes must be preserved. Return 2-3 strongest observations with exact file:line evidence, practical explanation, caveats. Distinguish a small useful helper from a costly abstraction and large internals from a leaky interface. Avoid unsupported scores. Focus on SettingsStore, PNGMetadata, ScreenshotService, ScreenRecordingService and tiny helpers. Which hide useful details? Which require callers to coordinate details? Verify actual call sites, return balanced assessment. No need to run tests for read-only opinion.

## Return a handoff to the orchestrator

You are an external worker. Complete the assignment above within its constraints.
Your final response must be one JSON object with the fields below. Put any
requested exact answer or payload in summary or findings. Keep it concise but
retain details needed to use and verify your work. Use empty arrays when a field
has no entries. Do not invent evidence, file locations, checks, or success.

{
  "outcome": "complete | partial | blocked",
  "summary": "The result and what it means for the assignment.",
  "findings": ["Concrete findings, including relevant exact values."],
  "changes": ["Files/artifacts changed and what changed; no unrelated files."],
  "decisions": ["Important choices and brief rationale, including rejected alternatives when useful."],
  "evidence": ["Exact source file paths and line numbers when known, URLs, reproduction steps, or artifact paths supporting the findings."],
  "checks": [{"check": "Actual command or verification", "result": "passed | failed | not_run", "detail": "Observed result, or why it was not run."}],
  "open_issues": ["Uncertainties, assumptions needing confirmation, blockers, missing checks, and questions for the orchestrator."],
  "next_steps": ["Specific remaining actions or integration guidance, if any."]
}

Report failed checks even if later corrected; say what fixed them. Distinguish
observed facts from hypotheses. For blocked or partial work, explain what is
missing and what would unblock it. Include important discoveries that affect
other work. Do not include private reasoning transcripts or routine tool chatter.
I'll inspect SettingsStore, PNGMetadata, ScreenshotService, ScreenRecordingService, and their real call sites to judge deep vs shallow modules from the code, not the floorplan.

text: PNGMetadata callers decide policy, such as which payload to embed and byte caps. This is sound layering, not a leak of chunk format. No unsupported scores were found. Tests were not run as requested. The outcome is complete with no changes.

{
  "outcome": "complete",
  "summary": "Call-site review (not floorplan/line-count): Zoomies has real deep modules—especially PNGMetadata, and to a large extent ScreenRecordingService and SettingsStore—plus a leaky shared encoding helper around screenshots. Tiny helpers like UniqueFileURLLogic are useful, not costly abstractions.",
  "findings": [
    "PNGMetadata is the clearest deep module: callers only call embed/extract/extractEditorState/isPNG; chunk parsing, iTXt assembly, CRC, and Zoomies-chunk stripping stay inside Sources/PNGMetadata.swift. Production callers: WorkflowImagePersistenceLogic (embed) and WorkflowReopenMetadataLogic (extract). Callers still choose *policy* (when to embed prompt+original vs editorState-only; 50MB skip in WorkflowImagePersistenceLogic)—that is layering, not a leak of PNG format.",
    "ScreenRecordingService and SettingsStore hide useful complexity behind narrow interfaces. AppDelegate/Tray drive recording with start/stop/state/elapsed/callbacks and never touch SCStream/session/finalize. Settings callers use load/settings/update/didRepair; path migration, JSON, normalization, and atomic writes stay private. UniqueFileURLLogic is the contrast case: a small useful helper (unique _2/_3 names), reused by recording/screenshot/clipboard/scratchpad—not a costly abstraction.",
    "ScreenshotService’s hotkey surface is relatively deep (captureArea/captureFullScreen hide ScreenCaptureKit, save, sound, workflow kickoff), but ScreenshotServiceCoreLogic is a leaky shared kitchen: EditorCanvasView, ScreenshotWorkflowController, WorkflowReopenMetadataLogic, and WorkflowImagePersistenceLogic must call pngData/bitmapRepresentation themselves. beginPostCaptureFlow’s fat overload also forces coordination of initialImage / persistence Task / counter. Large ScreenRecordingService internals alone would not prove depth; depth here is evidenced by the simple caller surface."
  ],
  "changes": [],
  "decisions": [
    "Judged depth from verified call sites and what callers must know, not file size or work/code-views floorplan grouping.",
    "Treated UniqueFileURLLogic/DirectoryPurgeLogic-style enums as small useful helpers; treated ScreenshotServiceCoreLogic as a leaky shared encoding surface rather than a deep module boundary.",
    "Did not assign numeric depth scores; assessment is qualitative with file:line evidence only."
  ],
  "evidence": [
    "Sources/PNGMetadata.swift:25-41 embed(original+prompt[+editorState]); 44-56 embed(editorState); 60-107 extract; 109-138 extractEditorState; private chunk/CRC ~147-336",
    "Sources/WorkflowImagePersistenceLogic.swift:31-41 PNGMetadata.embed only; 11-14 maxEmbeddedOriginalBytes policy outside PNGMetadata",
    "Sources/WorkflowReopenMetadataLogic.swift:58-59 extractEditorState + extract; 25 ScreenshotServiceCoreLogic.pngData for fresh capture",
    "Sources/SettingsStore.swift:50-73 load (legacy path + repair); 96-100 update; 104-126 private persist/loadSettings",
    "Sources/AppDelegate.swift:21 load; 101 didRepair; 125/162 settings reads; callers never call persist",
    "Sources/ScreenRecordingService.swift:92-127 start/stop; 39-55 state/elapsed/busy/onUpdate/onRecordingSaved; internals makeSession/finalize/monitor ~195-530",
    "Sources/AppDelegate.swift:40-45,89-97,134-162,146-147 recording call sites; Sources/TrayService.swift:35-48 state+elapsed only",
    "Sources/ScreenshotService.swift:71-103 captureArea; 134-185 beginPostCaptureFlow overload with persistence Task; 347-361 wrappers into CoreLogic",
    "ScreenshotServiceCoreLogic call sites outside ScreenshotService: Sources/EditorCanvasView.swift:302,1883; Sources/ScreenshotWorkflowController.swift:520,590; Sources/WorkflowReopenMetadataLogic.swift:25; Sources/WorkflowImagePersistenceLogic.swift:26",
    "Sources/UniqueFileURLLogic.swift:3-30; used from ScreenRecordingService.swift:331 and ScreenshotServiceCoreLogic.swift:81"
  ],
  "checks": [
    {
      "check": "Static read of Sources/* and grep of call sites for SettingsStore, PNGMetadata, ScreenshotService/CoreLogic, ScreenRecordingService, UniqueFileURLLogic",
      "result": "passed",
      "detail": "Call sites verified under Sources/; test files noted but not treated as production boundaries."
    },
    {
      "check": "Unit/integration test run",
      "result": "not_run",
      "detail": "User requested read-only opinion without tests."
    }
  ],
  "open_issues": [
    "AppDelegate busy-state orchestration across screenshot/recording/scratchpad/video-rename is cross-feature coordination, not a leak of ScreenRecordingService internals—worth not conflating with module depth.",
    "SettingsStore does not hide the Settings schema; UI and services still know field names—depth is about persistence/migration, not domain model encapsulation.",
    "Hypothesis only: further extraction of a single ‘image encode + metadata’ facade might deepen the screenshot boundary; not verified as net win."
  ],
  "next_steps": [
    "If orchestrating follow-up design: preserve PNGMetadata’s simple embed/extract surface; avoid treating CoreLogic reuse as proof of a clean ScreenshotService boundary.",
    "No code changes required from this review; existing user work left untouched."
  ]
}
